**dsa-explain** is a collection of short, visual, interactive lessons
on data structures and algorithms. Each module aims to build intuition
first through animation and direct manipulation before it asks a
reader to look at code.

The site is currently a scaffold: the navigation, layout, and design
system are in place, and each module page is a placeholder waiting for
content. See the [module grid](index.qmd) for the current roadmap.

**dsa-explain** project is supported by UBC OER grant

## A note on inspiration and attribution

The idea of a free, visual, self-contained explainer for a technical
topic owes a real debt to [MLU-Explain](https://mlu-explain.github.io/),
Amazon's collection of machine-learning explainers ([source on
GitHub](https://github.com/aws-samples/aws-mlu-explain)). We admire
that project's format: short, focused, one-idea-per-page lessons built
around an interactive visual.

This site's visual structure of navy-ink text and borders, flat/
sharp-edged cards, and a "highlighter" mark behind key text and
buttons was deliberately designed to feel close to MLU-Explain's.
The accent color, though, is a deliberate departure: a cool cobalt
blue rather than their warm coral/orange, chosen specifically so the
two sites read as clearly distinct at a glance. No CSS, font files,
illustrations, or written content from MLU-Explain were copied into
this project: every rule in
[`theme.scss`](https://github.com/your-username/dsa-explain/blob/main/theme.scss)
was written from scratch, and the typefaces here (Archivo and
JetBrains Mono) are open, freely-licensed Google Fonts chosen to
evoke the mood of Amazon's proprietary Ember typeface without using
it. MLU-Explain's own codebase remains under its own license — see
the original, linked above, for the real thing.

Unless noted otherwise on an individual page, written content on this
site is shared under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/),
and the site's own source code (Quarto config, theme, and scaffolding)
is available in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/dsa-explain/dsa-explain.github.io) under the MIT license.
